entries.evidence1318: The westernmost Asian elephants (Syrian elephant of Syria/Upper Mesopotamia) were hunted out by c. 100 BC; there are no medieval elephants in Iran, Iraq, Kuwait or Syria-Lebanon. China: elephants had left north China by the Zhou period and by the Song (960-1279) had shrunk to the far south (Guangdong, Guangxi, southern Fujian, southern Yunnan), retreating to Yunnan only under the Ming-Qing. The boxes therefore keep CHS/CHC south of about 25.5N. India: Babur (1520s) placed the western edge of wild elephants at the Kalpi country, so the Indus plain, Punjab and the Thar (PAK, the IND box, WHM) were already empty, while the rest of India and mainland Southeast Asia lost elephants after 1500. Borneo: the elephant is confined to the northeast with a single prehistoric tooth record, so the cells outside today's range are excluded. Philippines: Sulu elephants were at most a royal introduction. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_elephant https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1nq9mw https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6955318 https://scroll.in/article/1054424/illustrations-birds-and-animals-of-hindustan-from-the-pages-of-baburnama https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5772424

entries.evidence1318: Most continental losses are 17th-20th c. (France/Germany/Alps 19th-early 20th c.); in Iberia the Eurasian lynx survived in the Atlantic north and Pyrenees until the early 19th c. Losses in northeast and north China, Korea, Mongolia and the Himalaya (Ladakh, Gilgit, Nepal Trans-Himalaya) are 20th century. The Arctic boxes drop the treeless Taymyr and north Yakutian tundra beyond the forest-tundra. entries.note: Domestic dog. Decision 0054 (the author: domestic animals went wild when people disappeared): where people kept dogs around 1318, the same range in every profile (no PHYLACINE raster). Old World: the 1318 chicken regions without the small oceanic islands where dogs are not attested or were gone at contact (Easter Island, Samoa, Tonga, New Caledonia, Fiji, Vanuatu, the Solomons east of the Bismarcks, Micronesia, the Cooks, Australs, Marquesas, Pitcairn, Tokelau, Tuvalu, Wallis-Futuna, Niue, Laccadives, Maldives, Comoros, Socotra), plus Siberia and the Russian Far East. Americas: North America with the Arctic and Greenland (Thule and Norse dogs), Mexico, Central America, the Caribbean, the Andes, the Pampas, Paraguay and southern Brazil. New Zealand: the kuri arrived with people around 1300. Left out (no dogs or not attested in 1318; fails closed): Australia and Tasmania (the dingo is its own rule), Amazonia and the Guianas, northern and central Brazil, Patagonia and southern Chile (the Fuegian dog was a tamed culpeo), the Aleutians, the Andamans and islands uninhabited in 1318. Caninae 1.1.10 gives its dogs no natural spawn chance (puppies come from traders), so the rule matters only if a later provider version lets them spawn.
